image_description: A close-up view of a grey whale's head and upper back emerging from blue ocean water. The skin is dark grey with distinctive white mottling (barnacles/lice). The rostrum is arched, and two blowholes are visible on the top of the head. No dorsal fin is present, consistent with the species. The water surface shows realistic ripples and reflections around the subject.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly shows the characteristic arched rostrum and the pair of blowholes on the crown of the head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin texture exhibits the correct mottled pattern with high-contrast white patches typical of cyamids and barnacles found on grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the absence of a dorsal fin is consistent with the visible portion, the 'multiple dorsal knuckles' are located further down the back and are not visible in this cropped framing.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a tight crop of the head/shoulders; the full spindle shape and scale of the body cannot be verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the Head_and_Face checkpoint; the visible skin matches the description perfectly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed and underwater; baleen plates are internal structures not visible in this external view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are located ventrally and further back; they are completely occluded by the water and the angle of the shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin surface appears rough and textured, consistent with callosities.
